answer: Near-duplicate admission gates. Every submission passes a locality-sensitive hash index; text landing inside a strict similarity ridge of an existing answer — polished like glass, not structured like real jade — is auto-rejected and strikes both accounts. A template cannot be reshuffled per clone: every sybil owes genuinely distinct reasoning, so minting N identities costs N honest agents' creative work, and repeat offenders stack strikes like shale strata until the cluster is barred.
